profile.campus: True North Data campus, Loudoun County, VA (Loudoun County zoning case ZMAP-2017-0003, PIN 194103673000, approved Jan 2018)
profile.reading: This building sits at 42255 Thunderball Drive in Leesburg, Virginia, part of a data center campus that Loudoun County own zoning and permitting records identify by the project name True North Data. Loudoun County zoning case ZMAP-2017-0003, filed under that project name, rezoned roughly 105 acres to Planned Development-Office Park specifically to allow data center uses, and was approved January 18, 2018. The underlying parcel, county PIN 194103673000, covering roughly 97 acres, is recorded under a condominium-regime plat named True North Land Condo, a legal structure commonly used to subdivide one large hyperscale campus parcel into separately titled buildings, consistent with the six separate addresses and building records that make up this cluster. A 2019 grading permit for a project called True North 2 described three data center buildings with utilities, and a 2023 stormwater permit for True North Data Phase 2A covered a further 16.5 acres of disturbed area, indicating a phased expansion. Four tenant fit-up zoning permits were issued across April and May 2025, suggesting the campus was still being built out in phases as recently as that year. No document reviewed this session, however, gives a total megawatt capacity, final building count, or total square footage for the completed campus, and the identity of the corporate entity that actually filed the original 2017 rezoning application is not exposed in the county public zoning-case layer, so True North Data Solutions, the name this record carries as operator, could not be independently confirmed as a registered company through the Virginia State Corporation Commission this session. Loudoun County is widely described as the largest data center market in the world by capacity, and Leesburg location within it, near the eastern edge of the county fiber and power-dense corridor, is consistent with why a developer would pursue a multi-building campus of this scale here specifically.

profile.research_note: True North Data Solutions' own site publishes only company-wide totals ("10+ project sites," "673 MW capacity & growing" across 3 countries) with no facility-specific pages or addresses -- corporate office listed is in Calgary, AB. This Leesburg/Loudoun County VA campus (off Thunderball Drive) is reported in local press as a build-to-suit project (Compass Datacenters broke ground for True North); no public per-building spec sheet exists. One row on file is separately named "TikTok Data Center," consistent with reporting that this campus is a single-tenant build-to-suit, which explains the absence of public marketing specs.

reading.body:
This facility sits on a roughly 97-acre parcel in Leesburg rezoned in 2018 for data center use as part of what county records identify as the True North Data campus. Zoning and permitting documents from 2019 and 2023 describe multiple buildings under construction in phases, with tenant fit-up permits issued as recently as April and May 2025, indicating the campus was still being built out. The operator, True North Data Solutions, publishes only company-wide totals—673 MW across 10+ sites globally—and does not publish a megawatt figure specific to this location.

No public specification sheet exists for this building, and county records do not disclose total capacity or final building count for the campus. The operator's corporate website is currently inactive. Local reporting identifies this as a single-tenant build-to-suit project, which explains the absence of published specs typical of multi-tenant operator marketing. Without a published megawatt figure, this facility cannot be ranked among Virginia's 23 facilities with disclosed capacity.

Loudoun County, where this campus sits, is the largest data center market in the world by published capacity. This campus's location in Leesburg, near the eastern edge of the county's fiber and power corridor, places it within the geography where major infrastructure investment concentrates. The lack of any published power specification for a multi-building campus under construction through 2025 means its ultimate scale and timing remain opaque to public assessment.
